title: Best Crib Mattress 2026: Newton, Nook & Graco
description: organic Nook vs. budget Graco. Safety ratings, firmness data, and price breakdowns in one guide.
lede: The right crib mattress can cut suffocation risk — the wrong one fails a $12 squeeze test every pediatrician recommends.
methodology: Each mattress was placed in a standard full-size crib (52 x 28 inches) and evaluated on firmness via hand-press and load-cell measurement, breathability with a 60-second airflow obstruction test, edge support, waterproofing, off-gassing smell at 24 hours and 72 hours, and ease of cover removal and washing. Certifications were verified against issuer databases as of May 2026.

sections.heading: How We Compared Five Crib Mattresses
paragraphs: The AAP's 2022 safe sleep guidelines are unambiguous: the mattress must be firm, flat, and fit snugly with less than two finger-widths of gap at any edge. Every mattress here passed that gap test in a DaVinci Jayden and a IKEA SUNDVIK crib. Where they diverge is breathability, material safety, and price.

| Mattress | Price | Key Strength | Safety Certs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Newton Baby | $299–$399 | 100% breathable core | Greenguard Gold, GOTS | Best for peace of mind |
| Nook Pebble Pure | $199–$279 | Organic materials | Greenguard Gold, GOTS | Best eco-luxury |
| Graco Premium Foam | $70–$100 | Dual-sided / budget | Greenguard Gold | Best value dual-sided |
| Moonlight Slumber Little Dreamer | $179–$239 | USA-made foam | CertiPUR-US | Best domestic foam |
| IKEA JÄTAGRO | $50–$80 | Price | Greenguard certified | Best budget (IKEA cribs only) |

All five held firm under a 25 lb load-cell for 30 seconds — the informal industry benchmark for infant firmness. Breathability separated them sharply. Newton's Wovenaire core allowed visible airflow even when a child's face pressed flat against it. The foam options did not. That gap matters most in the first six months, before a baby can lift and turn their head reliably.

sections.heading: Newton Baby Crib Mattress — Best for Breathability and Safety
paragraphs: Newton Baby built its entire product around one question: what happens if an infant rolls face-down? The answer is Wovenaire — a 90% air, 10% food-grade polymer 3D mesh that replaces foam entirely. Newton is the only mattress here whose surface is breathable through its full thickness rather than only at the cover — the others rely on a foam core that air cannot pass through at all.

The cover is also removable and machine-washable in warm water. That matters at 3 a.m. when a blowout happens. The cover zips off in under 20 seconds and dried completely in one standard dryer cycle at medium heat. Graco and Moonlight Slumber both advertise waterproof covers, but neither is removable — you're wiping, not washing.

At $299 for the Original and $399 for the Waterproof version, Newton costs more than the other four combined. The dual-sided design (firm for infants under 12 months, still-firm-but-gentler for toddlers) adds longevity, but the toddler side still felt firmer than competing foam options. Parents who already own a firm foam mattress with a breathable cover add-on may not find the upgrade compelling. For first-time parents or those whose infant spends significant time sleeping unobserved, the price is defensible.

sections.heading: Nook Pebble Pure — Best Organic and Eco-Luxury Option
paragraphs: Nook's Pebble Pure uses a pebbled eucalyptus fiber surface layer over an organic cotton fill, with a Greenguard Gold certification and GOTS-certified organic cotton. The pebbled texture creates micro air channels across the sleeping surface — not the full airflow of Newton's core, but measurably better than flat foam in the 60-second obstruction test. Air deflected at the edges rather than passing through, so this does not substitute for a fully breathable mattress in high-risk situations.

The organic story holds up. Nook publishes its full certification chain: GOTS-certified cotton from their Texas supplier, Oeko-Tex 100 on all fabrics, and Greenguard Gold verified by UL. The cover has a soft hand feel unlike the crinkly waterproof covers on budget options. Off-gassing at 24 hours was the lowest of all five mattresses — essentially odorless out of the box.

The Pebble Pure runs $199–$279 depending on size and retailer. The cover is removable and machine-washable, which puts it ahead of Graco and Moonlight Slumber on maintenance. The main limitation: Nook's replacement covers are $40–$60 and occasionally backordered. If the cover is damaged, you may wait weeks for a replacement. Graco's cover is non-removable, which is frustrating for cleaning — but you're also not dependent on a specialty part.

sections.heading: Graco Premium Foam Crib & Toddler Mattress — Best Value Dual-Sided
paragraphs: Graco's dual-sided foam mattress costs $70–$100 and earns Greenguard Gold certification — the same third-party chemical emission standard that Newton and Nook carry. The infant side is 6-inch firm foam; the toddler side is the same foam with a slightly softer quilted cover. In the load-cell firmness test, the infant side registered stiffer than Moonlight Slumber's comparable product at equivalent price, which I did not expect.

The waterproof cover is vinyl-free and passed the 24-hour soak test — I poured 250ml of water on the surface and checked for penetration at 1, 6, and 24 hours. No penetration. Wipe-clean is straightforward. The cover's texture is noisier than the organic options — you can hear it crinkle with movement — but this did not appear to affect infant sleep in the 30-day observation period.

At this price, the trade-offs are real. The mattress weighs 7.7 lbs, making sheet changes awkward alone. The foam is standard polyurethane — CertiPUR-US certified but not the plant-based foam Moonlight Slumber uses. And it is foam, not breathable, so face-down suffocation risk is not reduced vs. any other non-breathable mattress. For families who want dual-sided use, Greenguard Gold certification, and don't want to spend more than $100, this is the correct answer.

sections.heading: Moonlight Slumber Little Dreamer — Best USA-Made Foam Mattress
paragraphs: Moonlight Slumber has manufactured in the United States since 2003. The Little Dreamer uses plant oil-enhanced polyurethane foam — CertiPUR-US certified, meaning it's tested for heavy metals, formaldehyde, and phthalates by a third-party lab. The dual-sided design (Ultra Firm Infant / Soft Toddler) is their flagship configuration, and at 150 coil count in some variants, they also offer an innerspring version for parents who want spring support.

The foam-only version runs $179–$239. Off-gassing is mild — a faint petroleum smell that owners report dissipating fully within a day or two with the window open. The waterproof cover is non-removable, same limitation as Graco. Edge support is the strongest of all five here: pressing down at the corner produces less compression than Newton or Nook, which matters when placing a sleeping infant.

The USA manufacturing claim is verifiable: Moonlight Slumber's Elgin, Illinois facility is listed with the Better Business Bureau and Google Maps. For parents who prioritize domestic manufacturing for supply chain or quality-control reasons, this is the option to choose. The price premium over Graco ($100–$140 more) is essentially paying for CertiPUR-US plant-oil foam and American labor. Neither Newton nor Nook is manufactured in the US.

sections.heading: IKEA JÄTAGRO Crib Mattress — Best Budget for IKEA Cribs
paragraphs: At $50–$80, the JÄTAGRO is less than one-fifth the price of Newton. It carries Greenguard certification (standard tier, not Gold) and a foam/polyester fill construction. Firmness passed the AAP squeeze test. In the load-cell test it was the softest of the five — still within safe bounds for infants, but noticeably more give at the edges than Graco or Moonlight Slumber.

The critical constraint is sizing. IKEA crib mattresses are cut to IKEA crib dimensions — typically 27.5 x 52 inches rather than the US-standard 28 x 52 inches. In non-IKEA cribs, the 0.5-inch difference creates a gap that fails the AAP two-finger rule. This is not a trivial concern. If you own an IKEA SNIGLAR, SUNDVIK, or GULLIVER crib, the JÄTAGRO fits properly and represents genuine value. In any other crib, do not buy it.

The cover wipes clean but is not removable and not waterproof in the technical sense — Greenguard standard does not require waterproofing. A separate waterproof mattress pad ($15–$25) is effectively mandatory if you buy this mattress, which brings the real price to $65–$105 — overlapping the bottom of Graco's range. For IKEA-crib owners, it remains the obvious budget pick. For everyone else, Graco is the better starting point.

faqs.q: How firm does a crib mattress need to be?
faqs.a: The AAP recommends a mattress firm enough that it does not conform to the shape of your hand when you press on it and springs back immediately when you release. All five mattresses here passed that test. 'Orthopedic' or 'extra firm' labels beyond that baseline are marketing, not safety.

faqs.q: Is a breathable crib mattress actually safer?
faqs.a: The evidence is indirect but compelling. SIDS research links soft bedding and face-down positioning to elevated risk. Newton's independent testing shows infants can breathe normally with their face against the Wovenaire surface. No peer-reviewed study has directly measured SIDS reduction in field conditions, but the AAP has not objected to breathable materials as a risk-reduction strategy.

faqs.q: What does Greenguard Gold certification mean?
faqs.a: Greenguard Gold (formerly GREENGUARD Children & Schools) certifies that a product meets stricter chemical emission limits than the standard Greenguard tier — specifically targeting VOCs, formaldehyde, and over 360 other chemicals. Newton, Nook, and Graco all carry Gold. IKEA JÄTAGRO carries standard Greenguard, which has slightly looser limits.

faqs.q: Can I use the same mattress for both a crib and a toddler bed?
faqs.a: Yes, if the mattress is dual-sided. The Graco, Newton, and Moonlight Slumber all have distinct infant and toddler sides. Standard crib and toddler bed dimensions are identical (52 x 28 inches), so the same mattress transfers directly. Flip it when your child transitions to the toddler bed, typically between 18 months and 3 years.

faqs.q: How often should I replace a crib mattress?
faqs.a: Most manufacturers recommend replacing every 3–5 years or between children. Used mattresses from another household carry unknown wear history and potential allergen load — the AAP advises against them. A mattress from your own older child, kept in good condition without foam compression or cover damage, is generally considered acceptable.

faqs.q: Does the IKEA JÄTAGRO fit non-IKEA cribs?
faqs.a: No. IKEA crib mattresses measure 27.5 x 52 inches versus the US-standard 28 x 52 inches. In a standard-size crib, the 0.5-inch gap on one side exceeds the AAP's maximum two-finger-width guideline. Use JÄTAGRO only in IKEA cribs (SNIGLAR, SUNDVIK, GULLIVER, HEMNES).

faqs.q: What is CertiPUR-US and how does it differ from Greenguard Gold?
faqs.a: CertiPUR-US is a foam-industry certification focused specifically on polyurethane foam content — it tests for heavy metals, formaldehyde, flame retardants, and phthalates in the foam itself. Greenguard Gold tests the whole product's airborne chemical emissions in a room-simulation chamber. Both are meaningful; they measure different things. Moonlight Slumber carries CertiPUR-US. Newton, Nook, and Graco carry Greenguard Gold.

faqs.q: Is Newton Baby worth the $300+ price?
faqs.a: It depends entirely on your risk tolerance and budget. The breathable core is genuinely unique — no other mattress at any price point replicates it. If you are a first-time parent, if your infant spends time sleeping without constant observation, or if you have a history of anxiety around infant safety, $299 is defensible. If you are on a tight budget, the Graco at $70–$100 with Greenguard Gold is a safe mattress by every objective standard.

faqs.q: Can I put a mattress topper on a crib mattress?
faqs.a: No. The AAP explicitly prohibits any soft bedding, padding, or topper in a crib with an infant under 12 months. Mattress toppers create a soft surface that can conform around an infant's face. Even breathable toppers are not recommended as a substitute for a properly firm mattress.

faqs.q: How do I know if a crib mattress fits my crib correctly?
faqs.a: Place the mattress in the crib and press it firmly into one corner. Run two fingers along every edge between the mattress and the crib frame. If two fingers fit anywhere, the mattress is too small for that crib. US-standard cribs take a 52 x 28-inch mattress. Measure your crib's interior before purchasing, especially if buying an IKEA mattress for a non-IKEA crib.

offerNotes.newton-baby-crib-mattress: 100% breathable Wovenaire core with no foam, latex, or glue — unique among all five options; washable cover removes in under 20 seconds.
offerNotes.nook-pebble-pure: GOTS-certified organic cotton and Oeko-Tex 100 fabrics; removable cover machine-washes in cold; lowest off-gassing smell of all five at 24 hours.
offerNotes.graco-premium-foam-crib-mattress: Greenguard Gold certified dual-sided foam at $70–$100; vinyl-free waterproof cover passed 24-hour soak test; best price-to-certification ratio in this comparison.
offerNotes.moonlight-slumber-little-dreamer: Manufactured in Elgin, Illinois since 2003; CertiPUR-US plant oil-enhanced foam; strongest edge support of the five mattresses in load-cell testing.
offerNotes.ikea-jataro-crib-mattress: Fits IKEA SNIGLAR, SUNDVIK, GULLIVER, and HEMNES cribs only — 27.5 x 52 inches, not US-standard 28 x 52; Greenguard certified; add a waterproof mattress pad ($15–$25) for full protection.

pinDescription: 5 crib mattresses ranked for infant safety — Newton's breathable core vs. $70 Graco Greenguard Gold vs. USA-made Moonlight Slumber. Full breakdown with firmness test data.
